newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu sees increased defence spending.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu sees increased defence spending.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in remarks published on Friday he wanted to increase substantially the Jewish state's defence budget.

"I believe that in the future, after we stabilise the economy and put it back on the right track, we'll be able to substantially increase the defence budget," the daily Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper quoted him as saying in an interview.
Israeli defence officials have recently said the army needs more money to prepare for the possibility of war with Syria, deemed more likely now than in recent years.
But army chief Lieutenant-General Amnon Shahak said on Friday Israel and Syria were not on the verge of war.

Shahak spoke to reporters a day after his deputy said Israel was taking into account the possibility of having to fight Syria in the coming year and was planning its training schedule according to that assessment.
"In my opinion we are not close to a war with Syria. We said the assessment of the situation had changed, not that we are on the verge of war," said Shahak.
"There are changes in the area and we are aware of them. They don't point to an immediate danger of war. That's not the picture at this moment."

Deputy army chief Matan Vilnai said on Thursday Israel was taking into account the possibility of having to fight Syria in the coming year and was planning its training scheduled according to that assessment.
Tensions between the countries soared in September when Syria moved thousands of its troops stationed in Lebanon to within striking range of Israeli army positions in the Golan Heights.
Damascus said the redeployment was defensive but some Israeli officials saw it as a prelude to war.

Earlier this week Israel's air force intelligence chief said the probability of war with the Arabs could no longer be characterised as low and that Damascus remained "Israel's number one confrontation state".
Israel and Syria launched peace talks in 1991 after fighting several wars but have failed to agree in sporadic negotiations on a formula for solving their dipute.
Syria wants back the Golan Heights which Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war. Netanyahu rejects the land-for-peace formula which has been the basis for five years of U.S.-sponsored talks.
Israel Radio said on Friday Syria had indicated to Israel through a French intermediary that it was ready to resume peace talks next month for the first time since Netanyahu was elected last May.
Israel's 1997 budget includes a slight increase in defence spending along with cuts in other spheres which Netanyahu has said are necessary to rein in the deficit.
Defence spending in 1997 will be 30.4 billion shekels ($9.2 billion), or about 16 percent of the total 188 billion shekel ($60 billion) budget.
